transcript:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2025-11-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Aurora - Head of ML), Kevin Chen (Aurora - Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Aurora - SRE)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we're excited to walk through Redwood's eval and quality monitoring flow today. i think ethan will take the demo, i'll chime in on commercial/security bits, sound good?
[00:18] Ethan: yep thanks samira, morning everyone  um quick agenda, i'll show Console -> Optimize eval flow, prompt set creation, how we do A/B comparisons, and then regression alerts and integration points into CI.
[00:30] Maya: great, we mainly care about catching regressions when we swap model versions and automated alerts; also want a clear way to compare outputs across models for our critical prompts.
[00:45] Kevin: and cost matters  we currently run 3 models in prod and want to limit token spend. we'll want to see how batching/quantization suggestions impact quality.
[01:00] Ethan: totally. opening the Console  this is the Eval tab. you can import prompt sets as CSV or via API; many teams keep canonical prompts per intent. quick note: sometimes our transcription shows product names weirdly, but this is the real UI.
[01:20] Ethan: (click) here i uploaded two prompt sets  "billing-intent" and "account-recovery" — each with expected outputs and rubric. you can see baseline metrics (exact match, F1, semantic similarity) and we store historical evaluations.
[01:40] Priya: how are rubrics defined? can we do custom scorers or must it be built-in metrics?
[01:50] Ethan: you can plug custom scorers via a webhook or run a local scorer in your CI. Optimize has an operator to run our built-in metrics or call your scorer (we've seen teams use wer/bleu/emb-sim combos).
[02:10] Maya: and for A/B  do you spin parallel requests or replay logs?
[02:18] Ethan: both options. for live traffic we have a routing policy to split requests (A/B by percentage). for offline analysis you can replay logs or run the eval harness against a batch of past queries.
[02:35] Kevin: what's the latency impact when running A/B in prod?
[02:40] Ethan: minimal if you route to compatible model variants; for true dual-call A/B there is cost/latency overhead, but we also recommend offline replay or async comparisons. also Redwood Optimize suggests batching profiles so you can keep latency SLOs.
[03:00] Samira: from a procurement angle we provide Dedicated and Private options  Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and isolation; Private gives VPC/on-prem and KMS integration.
[03:15] Priya: on KMS  do you integrate with customer-managed keys or do you only support Redwood KMS?
[03:22] Samira: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and have HSM integrations for enterprise. for Hosted we use our KMS but can negotiate key handling for contracts.
[03:35] Maya: okay that's promising. next, can you show an example of a regression alert?
[03:42] Ethan: sure  here's a regression rule we created: if semantic similarity drops by >0.08 or F1 drops >5% vs pinned baseline, fire an alert. alerts can route to Slack, PagerDuty, or create a ticket in JIRA.
[04:00] Ethan: (types) i'm going to force a simulated regression  you'll see the alert page populate with the failing prompt examples and model diffs side-by-side. note: sometimes NER labels get munged in transcripts, but the UI shows clean diffs.
[04:25] Kevin: nice  can we attach custom context (like user signals) to help triage?
[04:30] Ethan: yes, eval results include request metadata and you can surface upstream features; we also store KV cache hits and prefix info if you use our runtime.
[04:50] Maya: about A/B comparisons  how are differences summarized? is it automatic scoring + human review queue?
[04:58] Ethan: automatic scoring first; then you can flag examples for manual review. the Console has a human review workflow where you can label issues and tag examples to retrain or create new prompt templates.
[05:20] Priya: big question on data residency  we have EU customers, do you support region-restricted eval storage?
[05:28] Samira: yes, for Dedicated/Private you can pin region and data residency; hosted customers can request region controls for enterprise plans. we also provide audit logs per token and per-eval run.
[05:45] Maya: what about integrating evals into CI? we want to gate deploys on regression thresholds.
[05:52] Ethan: we have a CLI and API that your pipeline can call to run evals pre-deploy. many customers add a step: run eval against canonical prompt set, fail if regression rule triggers. we also push metrics to Prometheus/Datadog via exporter.
[06:20] Kevin: ok, cost again  how do you estimate cost of continuous evals?
[06:26] Ethan: Console shows token estimates per eval run; Optimize suggests sampling + caching to cut cost. you can also set sampling strategies: e.g., 10% live samples + weekly full runs.
[06:45] Maya: if we pin a model baseline, can we still run nightly comparisons against new open models?
[06:51] Ethan: yep, you can pin baseline and schedule nightly jobs to evaluate candidate models; our model catalog includes quantized variants and we automatically surface compatible fallbacks to meet SLOs.
[07:10] Kevin: you mentioned model catalog  can we onboard our own custom model?
[07:14] Ethan: absolutely. you can upload weights to Private or point Dedicated to your image; we include kernel selection and quantization suggestions. small hiccup sometimes the model name gets changed in transcripts but it works fine in the Console.
[07:35] Samira: i want to call out success criteria  what would make this pilot successful for you?
[07:40] Maya: reduce regression noise  we want meaningful alerts that catch real quality drops and reduce manual triage by at least 50%.
[07:48] Kevin: and measurable cost savings vs our current approach, plus smooth integration into CI.
[07:55] Priya: and security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration without complex network changes.
[08:05] Ethan: noted. demo continuing  here is the A/B detail view: you can compare per-prompt scores, aggregate diffs, and view human annotations. i'll open an example where Model A paraphrases incorrectly and Model B is correct; you can tag that example to create a new prompt or add it to training set.
[08:35] Maya: do you support multi-metric alerting? e.g., only alert if both semantic sim and a rubric fail?
[08:42] Ethan: yes, our alert rules support boolean combinations and severity levels. you can set immediate page or low-priority digest.
[09:00] Kevin: for pilot scope  what infra will we need? Dedicated sounds appealing but we need to size GPUs.
[09:08] Samira: we typically start with a small reserved pool (1-2 GPUs) for a pilot; Ethan can propose a sizing doc after he sees your throughput.
[09:18] Ethan: right, if you share qps and average seq length i'll run a cost/latency profile. Kevin, can you share those numbers after the call?
[09:25] Kevin: yes i'll put them in the doc.
[09:30] Maya: one more about alerts  can we integrate with our existing ticketing so every regression creates a pre-filled ticket with examples?
[09:36] Ethan: yup we have a JIRA integration template and payload you can customize.
[09:45] Priya: network  if we do Private, do you require a VPN tunnel, or can we use VPC peering?
[09:52] Samira: both supported; for on-prem we support air-gapped packages. we'll share the network runbook.
[10:05] Ethan: (navigates) now showing CI integration example: here's a GitHub Actions step that calls the eval API and fails the job if regression. many customers use this to gate deploys.
[10:25] Kevin: will you also store historical eval runs for audit?
[10:28] Ethan: yes, retention is configurable; enterprise plans can increase retention and export to S3 or customer storage.
[10:40] Maya: what's the turnaround on security review normally? we have a procurement window of ~3-4 weeks.
[10:46] Samira: typical enterprise security review is 2-4 weeks depending on controls; we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and a mini-architecture review.
[11:00] Maya: ok, perfect. can we talk about demo-specific pilot  two prompt sets, nightly evals, regression alerts to Slack, and a JIRA ticket per high-severity regression?
[11:08] Ethan: sounds good. i'll run an initial bench comparing your current model and a quantized candidate and share diffs.
[11:15] Samira: i'll follow up with the pricing and the security pack.
[11:20] Maya: thanks, this was helpful  one little thing: are there sample notebooks to show how to format prompt sets?
[11:26] Ethan: yes, we have a repo and a quickstart notebook; i'll add the link. sometimes the file names in transcripts are slightly off but links will be accurate.
[11:40] Kevin: timeline  we aim to start a pilot early december.
[11:44] Samira: great, we'll target the week of 2025-12-08.
[11:50] Priya: thanks everyone, look forward to the runbook and next steps.
[11:55] Samira: recap: Samira send security + pricing, Ethan bench + sample notebooks, Aurora share prompts + qps numbers; follow-up meeting 2025-12-10.
[12:05] Maya: thanks all.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
